note: Butorides atricapilla (avibase-7085B8A0). The African Little Heron is the regional member of the historical striata/atricapilla complex; eBird v2026 restricts B. striata to the Americas. Africa-wide range inference from eBird/Clements v2026 and Avibase; not a record-level identification, and unusual vagrancy is possible.

Pogoniulus uropygialis (avibase-E01F4BD7). Northern Red-fronted Tinkerbird occurs in Kenya; the southern member is described from Mozambique and South Africa. The historical code and split need review. Based on eBird/Clements v2026 range descriptions and the Avibase Kenya checklist; a range-based inference, not record-level identification. Applied to the EAC and Horn of Africa: the other member is outside these countries in the published range; this is a regional inference, not a record identification.

Ptyonoprogne rufigula (avibase-A85102D3). Red-throated Crag-Martin is on the Kenya checklist; the southern member has a southern African range. Historical migrant or out-of-range records are not excluded. Based on eBird/Clements v2026 range descriptions and the Avibase Kenya checklist; a range-based inference, not record-level identification. Applied to the EAC and Horn of Africa: the other member is outside these countries in the published range; this is a regional inference, not a record identification.

Trachylaemus purpuratus (avibase-80BC978E). Eastern Yellow-billed Barbet occurs in Kenya; T. goffinii is described from West Africa. Based on eBird/Clements v2026 range descriptions and the Avibase Kenya checklist; a range-based inference, not record-level identification. Applied to the EAC and Horn of Africa: the other member is outside these countries in the published range; this is a regional inference, not a record identification.

Apalis stronachi (avibase-DCA0028B). Maasai Apalis occurs in southwestern Kenya; A. karamojae is described from northeastern Uganda. The old KBM code represents the wider split. Based on eBird/Clements v2026 range descriptions and the Avibase Kenya checklist; a range-based inference, not record-level identification.

Zosterops kaffensis (avibase-52C60399). Kafa White-eye is described from Mount Kulal in northern Kenya; Z. poliogastrus is described from Ethiopia and South Sudan. Check that the historical KBM concept excludes other splits. Based on eBird/Clements v2026 range descriptions and the Avibase Kenya checklist; a range-based inference, not record-level identification.

Zosterops senegalensis (avibase-86F34425). The Northern Yellow White-eye range includes Kenya; Z. kasaicus is described from central Africa. Based on eBird/Clements v2026 range descriptions and the Avibase Kenya checklist; a range-based inference, not record-level identification.

Ardea brachyrhyncha (avibase-C3ABF863). The African taxon is the regional candidate for the old Intermediate Egret complex; A. intermedia and A. plumifera have Asian/Australasian published ranges. Africa-wide range inference from eBird/Clements v2026 and Avibase; not a record-level identification, and unusual vagrancy is possible.

Ciconia microscelis (avibase-5157C558). The African Woolly-necked Stork is the regional candidate; eBird v2026 restricts C. episcopus to Asia. Africa-wide range inference from eBird/Clements v2026 and Avibase; not a record-level identification, and unusual vagrancy is possible.

Brown/Cocos Booby complex: Brown Booby Sula leucogaster is widespread on African coasts and islands; S. brewsteri breeds in the eastern Pacific. Assume the common African member; unusual vagrancy is possible. https://avibase.ca/5EC21767

European/Grey-crowned Goldfinch complex: Carduelis carduelis occurs in northwestern Africa and Egypt; C. caniceps is described from central and southern Asia. Assume the common African member; unusual vagrancy is possible. https://avibase.ca/1B235E00

Southern/Western Rockhopper Penguin complex: Eudyptes filholi breeds on South Africa’s Prince Edward Islands and other southern Indian Ocean islands; E. chrysocome breeds in southern South America and winters along Patagonia. Assume the African-region member; pelagic vagrancy is possible. https://avibase.ca/4023CC81

White-throated/Angola Greenbul complex: P. albigularis occurs in the DRC, South Sudan and Uganda; P. viridiceps is described from northwestern Angola. Assumes the common EAC and Horn member; vagrancy and ID error remain possible. https://avibase.ca/D4CB1B89

Velvet-mantled/Fanti Drongo complex: the coracinus group occurs from the Congo basin to South Sudan, Kenya and Rwanda; the atactus group is West African and the nominate group is on Príncipe. This eBird group is a regional assumption, not a subspecies identification. https://avibase.ca/5DEB4565

Cameroon/Evergreen Forest Warbler complex: the eBird mariae group includes the Kenyan mariae and usambarae populations; other lopezi groups include western and central African taxa. Assumes the common Kenyan group, not a confirmed identification. https://avibase.ca/8160D091

Marsh/Anchieta's Tchagra complex: eBird/Clements v2026 places B. minuta minuta in Kenya, while anchietae and reichenowi are described from southern DRC and/or Tanzania southward. Assumes the common Kenyan taxon; unusual range changes or vagrancy remain possible. https://avibase.ca/7DCA1C1E

User identifies Agapornis hybrid in East Africa and Kenya as Fischer’s x Yellow-collared Lovebird (eBird x00671). Original KBM label does not specify parents and the older workbook has a conflicting Vanellus label; confirm historical source-code meaning.

Yellow-gorgeted/Pale-throated Greenbul complex: eBird/Clements v2026 places A. flavicollis in West Africa and A. flavigula across the Congo basin, South Sudan, Ethiopia and western Kenya. East African records are provisionally assigned to A. flavigula under the regional range assumption; unusual vagrancy remains possible. https://avibase.ca/C73137EA

Little Swift: the eBird affinis group includes affinis, aerobates, galilejensis and theresae; the v2026 ranges place African mainland birds in this group. The source concept is a different broad affinis treatment, so this is a provisional group-level assumption, not proof of an individual subspecies. https://avibase.ca/D209A90C https://avibase.ca/6B552CE9

Augur Buzzard: eBird/Clements v2026 describes Buteo augur augur from Ethiopian highlands south to Zimbabwe, while archeri is restricted to northern Somalia. Kenyan records are provisionally assigned to augur under the regional range assumption, not identified to subspecies in the original checklist. https://avibase.ca/EBDC03AA

Barn Swallow: eBird/Clements v2026 describes the rustica population as wintering in sub-Saharan Africa; other named groups primarily winter in Asia or the Americas. Assume the common Kenyan population; vagrants and records without subspecies identification remain possible. https://avibase.ca/58C502EA

Historical KBM code 234 is labelled Charadrius mongolus, but the 2024 crosswalk treats it as the former broad mongolus/atrifrons complex. The current source ID denotes the narrower Siberian Sand Plover; Tibetan Sand Plover A. atrifrons winters in eastern Africa while the listed mongolus range is eastern Asia and the Pacific. This override assumes the historical broad code, not that A. mongolus itself equals atrifrons. Review any post-split records and unusual vagrants. https://avibase.ca/8A4C4629

Rufous-naped Lark: eBird v2025 Corypha africana (runlar1) retired in v2026; Kenya EBD records mapped to the v2026 Corypha africana concept (runlar1) on user decision, 2026-11-04. Not used by ABAP preparation, whose source concept differs. https://avibase.ca/4E923B31 https://avibase.ca/EB9CE6A2

Rufous-naped Lark (Rufous-naped): eBird v2025 issf runlar5 retired in v2026; mapped to the v2026 species Corypha africana (runlar1), not to a v2026 group, on user decision, 2026-11-04. https://avibase.ca/6164890C https://avibase.ca/EB9CE6A2

ABAP Spp 458 Rufous-naped Lark (Corypha africana): mapped in Kenya to the eBird v2026 species Corypha africana (runlar1) on user decision, 2026-11-04, replacing the worldwide broad fallback to Corypha sp. Sentinel Lark (athi) records filed under this code would be misassigned. https://avibase.ca/6A0D6123 https://avibase.ca/EB9CE6A2
